payload.claim: The "Notes for the agent" / "The prose gate" paragraph tells the agent to avoid, in new prose, an em dash, a semicolon, a contraction, the perfect tense, or a sentence over 25 words, and to keep docstrings within ten lines, matching several of the repo's actual blocking `prose` gate rules. But that gate (`.saffron/gates/prose.py`) also blocks on a hedge-word rule (should/may/might), a filler-word list, and a mid-sentence if/when ("trailing-condition") construction, applied to every new comment and docstring the cell writes in `saffron/spec_citations.py`, none of which this note mentions. A careful build could still trip `prose` on one of the unmentioned rules with no warning from the spec.
